name: gitlab_access_request_approve_group
description:
Approve a group access request. Optionally set the access level (10=Guest, 20=Reporter, 30=Developer, 40=Maintainer).

See also: gitlab_access_request_list_group, gitlab_group_member_add

Returns: JSON with the approved access request details.

access_level.description: Access level to grant (5=Minimal access, 10=Guest, 15=Planner (Premium), 20=Reporter, 25=Security Manager (Premium), 30=Developer, 40=Maintainer, 50=Owner)

user_id.description: User ID of the access requester

name: gitlab_access_request_approve_project
description:
Approve a project access request. Optionally set the access level (10=Guest, 20=Reporter, 30=Developer, 40=Maintainer).

See also: gitlab_access_request_list_project, gitlab_project_member_add

Returns: JSON with the approved access request details.

access_level.description: Access level to grant (5=Minimal access, 10=Guest, 15=Planner (Premium), 20=Reporter, 25=Security Manager (Premium), 30=Developer, 40=Maintainer)

user_id.description: User ID of the access requester

name: gitlab_access_request_deny_group
description:
Deny a group access request. This action cannot be undone.

See also: gitlab_access_request_approve_group, gitlab_access_request_list_group

Returns: confirmation message.

confirm.description: Set true to explicitly confirm this destructive action instead of relying on MCP elicitation.

user_id.description: User ID of the access requester

name: gitlab_access_request_deny_project
description:
Deny a project access request. This action cannot be undone.

See also: gitlab_access_request_approve_project, gitlab_access_request_list_project

Returns: confirmation message.

confirm.description: Set true to explicitly confirm this destructive action instead of relying on MCP elicitation.

user_id.description: User ID of the access requester

name: gitlab_access_request_list_project
description: List pending access requests for a project. Returns: access requests with id, username, name, state, access level, requested/created timestamps, and pagination metadata. See also: gitlab_access_request_approve_project, gitlab_access_request_deny_project, gitlab_project_member_list.

name: gitlab_access_request_request_group
description:
Request access to a GitLab group for the authenticated user.

See also: gitlab_access_request_list_group, gitlab_group_member_add

Returns: JSON with the access request details.

name: gitlab_access_request_request_project
description:
Request access to a GitLab project for the authenticated user.

See also: gitlab_access_request_list_project, gitlab_project_member_add

Returns: JSON with the access request details.

name: gitlab_activate_user
description:
Activate a deactivated GitLab user (admin only). Deactivated users have been inactive and need reactivation.

See also: gitlab_deactivate_user, gitlab_get_user

Returns: JSON with action confirmation.

name: gitlab_add_commit_discussion_note
description:
Add a reply note to an existing commit discussion thread.

Returns: JSON with created note including ID, body, and author.

See also: gitlab_get_commit_discussion, gitlab_update_commit_discussion_note

name: gitlab_add_email
description:
Add an email address to the currently authenticated GitLab user.

See also: gitlab_list_emails, gitlab_delete_email

Returns: JSON with the created email details.

name: gitlab_add_email_for_user
description:
Add an email address to a specific GitLab user (admin only). Requires user ID and email address.

See also: gitlab_list_emails_for_user, gitlab_delete_email_for_user

Returns: JSON with the created email details.

name: gitlab_add_epic_discussion_note
description:
Add a reply note to an existing epic discussion thread via the Work Items GraphQL API.

Returns: JSON with created note including ID, body, and author.

See also: gitlab_get_epic_discussion, gitlab_update_epic_discussion_note

full_path.description: Full path of the group (e.g. my-group)

name: gitlab_add_gpg_key
description:
Add a GPG key to the currently authenticated GitLab user. Requires the armored GPG public key.

See also: gitlab_list_gpg_keys, gitlab_delete_gpg_key

Returns: JSON with the created GPG key details.

key.description: The armored GPG public key content

name: gitlab_add_gpg_key_for_user
description:
Add a GPG key to a specific GitLab user (admin only). Requires user ID and GPG public key.

See also: gitlab_list_gpg_keys_for_user, gitlab_delete_gpg_key_for_user

Returns: JSON with the created GPG key details.

key.description: The armored GPG public key content

name: gitlab_add_group_badge
description:
Add a new badge to a group. Badge URLs support placeholders like %{project_path}, %{default_branch}, %{commit_sha}.

See also: gitlab_list_group_badges, gitlab_preview_group_badge

Returns: JSON with the badge details.

name: gitlab_add_group_job_token_allowlist
description: Add a group to a project's CI/CD job token allowlist. Returns: the new allowlist entry with source project ID and target group ID. See also: gitlab_list_job_token_group_allowlist, gitlab_remove_group_job_token_allowlist, gitlab_add_project_job_token_allowlist.

target_group_id.description: ID of the group to add to the allowlist

name: gitlab_add_issue_discussion_note
description: Add a reply note to an existing issue discussion thread. Returns: the created note (author, body, timestamps). See also: gitlab_create_issue_discussion, gitlab_get_issue_discussion, gitlab_update_issue_discussion_note.

created_at.description: Backdate the note creation time (ISO 8601, e.g. 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z); requires admin or owner rights

name: gitlab_add_license
description: Add a GitLab Enterprise license. Returns: the installed license with plan, expiration, and entitlements. See also: gitlab_get_license, gitlab_delete_license.

name: gitlab_add_merge_request_to_merge_train
description:
Add a merge request to a merge train.

Returns: JSON array of merge train entries after the addition.

See also: gitlab_get_merge_request_on_merge_train, gitlab_list_project_merge_trains

sha.description: Head SHA of the merge request to verify

name: gitlab_add_project_badge
description:
Add a new badge to a project. Badge URLs support placeholders like %{project_path}, %{default_branch}, %{commit_sha}.

See also: gitlab_list_project_badges, gitlab_preview_project_badge

Returns: JSON with the badge details.

name: gitlab_add_project_job_token_allowlist
description: Add a project to a project's CI/CD job token inbound allowlist. Returns: the new allowlist entry with source and target project IDs. See also: gitlab_list_job_token_inbound_allowlist, gitlab_remove_project_job_token_allowlist, gitlab_add_group_job_token_allowlist.

target_project_id.description: ID of the project to add to the allowlist

name: gitlab_add_project_mirror
description: Create a push (remote) mirror on a project. Returns: the created mirror with id, enabled state, redacted URL, and update status. See also: gitlab_list_project_mirrors, gitlab_edit_project_mirror, gitlab_get_project_mirror_public_key.

host_keys.description: SSH host keys for the remote mirror

keep_divergent_refs.description: Keep divergent refs on the remote

mirror_branch_regex.description: Regex pattern for branches to mirror

url.description: Remote push mirror URL (e.g. https://user:token@example.com/repo.git). URL-embedded credentials are supported only for push mirrors; treat them as secrets, do not log or store them, and redact tokens or passwords in telemetry/errors

name: gitlab_add_snippet_discussion_note
description:
Add a reply note to an existing snippet discussion thread.

Returns: JSON with the created reply note.

See also: gitlab_get_snippet_discussion, gitlab_update_snippet_discussion_note

name: gitlab_add_ssh_key
description:
Add an SSH key to the currently authenticated GitLab user. Requires a title and the public key content.

See also: gitlab_list_ssh_keys, gitlab_delete_ssh_key

Returns: JSON with the created SSH key details.

title.description: A descriptive title for the SSH key

usage_type.description: Usage type: auth or signing (default: auth)

name: gitlab_add_ssh_key_for_user
description:
Add an SSH key to a specific GitLab user (admin only). Requires user ID, title, and public key content.

See also: gitlab_list_ssh_keys_for_user, gitlab_delete_ssh_key_for_user

Returns: JSON with the created SSH key details.

title.description: A descriptive title for the SSH key

usage_type.description: Usage type: auth or signing (default: auth)

name: gitlab_add_system_hook
description: Add an instance system hook. Returns: the created system hook with id, url, and triggers. See also: gitlab_edit_system_hook, gitlab_test_system_hook.

branch_filter_strategy.description: Branch filter strategy: wildcard, regex, or all_branches

enable_ssl_verification.description: Enable SSL verification for the hook URL

push_events_branch_filter.description: Branch filter for push events (wildcard, regex, or branch name)

signing_token.description: Write-only signing token for webhook signature validation

name: gitlab_approve_user
description:
Approve a pending GitLab user registration (admin only). Required when user sign-up requires admin approval.

See also: gitlab_reject_user, gitlab_list_users

Returns: JSON with action confirmation.

name: gitlab_ban_user
description:
Ban a GitLab user, hiding their activity and preventing login (admin only). More restrictive than blocking.

See also: gitlab_unban_user, gitlab_block_user

Returns: JSON with action confirmation.

confirm.description: Set true to explicitly confirm this destructive action instead of relying on MCP elicitation.

name: gitlab_block_user
description:
Block a GitLab user, preventing login and API access (admin only). The user's contributions remain intact.

See also: gitlab_unblock_user, gitlab_get_user

Returns: JSON with action confirmation.

confirm.description: Set true to explicitly confirm this destructive action instead of relying on MCP elicitation.

name: gitlab_board_create
description: Create a new issue board in a project. Returns: the created board with its project, scope, and lists. See also: gitlab_board_get, gitlab_board_update, gitlab_board_list.

name: gitlab_board_delete
description: Delete an issue board permanently. Returns: a success confirmation naming the board and project. See also: gitlab_board_get, gitlab_board_list.

confirm.description: Set true to explicitly confirm this destructive action instead of relying on MCP elicitation.

name: gitlab_board_get
description: Get a single issue board by board_id. Returns: the board with its project, milestone, assignee, scope labels, and ordered lists. See also: gitlab_board_list, gitlab_board_update, gitlab_board_delete.

name: gitlab_board_list

name: gitlab_board_list_create
description: Create a board list (column) scoped to a label, assignee, milestone, or iteration. Returns: the created list with its scope, position, and issue limits. See also: gitlab_board_list_get, gitlab_board_list_update, gitlab_board_list_lists.

name: gitlab_board_list_get

description: List the lists (columns) in an issue board with pagination. Returns: each list with its label, assignee, milestone, iteration, position, and issue limits. See also: gitlab_board_list_get, gitlab_board_list_create, gitlab_board_get.

name: gitlab_board_list_update
description: Reorder a board list to a new position. Returns: the updated list with its scope, position, and issue limits. See also: gitlab_board_list_get, gitlab_board_list_lists, gitlab_board_list_delete.

name: gitlab_board_update
description: Update an issue board's name, scope (assignee, milestone, labels, weight), or list visibility. Returns: the updated board with its project, scope, and lists. See also: gitlab_board_get, gitlab_board_delete, gitlab_board_list.

name: gitlab_branch_create
description: Create a branch from a source ref (branch, tag, or commit SHA). Returns: the created branch with its head commit object, protection and default flags, and web URL. See also: gitlab_branch_list, gitlab_merge_request_create, gitlab_repository_compare.

name: gitlab_branch_delete

description: Delete all branches merged into the default branch. Returns: a success confirmation. Protected and default branches are skipped. See also: gitlab_branch_list, gitlab_merge_request_list.

name: gitlab_branch_get

name: gitlab_bulk_update_security_attributes

name: gitlab_cancel_bulk_import

name: gitlab_change_plan_limits

name: gitlab_ci_lint

Validate arbitrary CI/CD YAML content within a project's namespace context. Useful for testing CI configuration changes before committing. Returns validation status, errors, warnings, and merged YAML.

name: gitlab_ci_lint_project
description:
Validate a project's CI/CD configuration (.gitlab-ci.yml) from the repository. Returns validation status, errors, warnings, merged YAML, and includes.

name: gitlab_discover_project
description:
Resolve a full git remote URL to a GitLab project and return its project_id and metadata. Read-only; performs a lookup against the GitLab Projects API; no side effects.

When to use: only when the user or workspace provides a complete git remote URL from .git/config ([remote "origin"] url = ...) or from 'git remote -v'. If the prompt already provides a project path such as group/project or a numeric project ID, pass that value directly as params.project_id to the requested GitLab tool instead of calling discovery. Do not synthesize, guess, or add .git to a project path to create a remote URL.
NOT for: searching projects by name (use gitlab_search action=projects), listing a user's projects (use gitlab_project action=list_user_projects), verifying GitLab connectivity or authentication (use gitlab_server action=health_check), or pre-checking workflows where project_id is already known.

IMPORTANT: pass the complete URL exactly as it appears — do NOT strip the git@ prefix from SSH URLs. Supported formats (a URL scheme or git@ user prefix is required):
- HTTPS: https://gitlab.example.com/group/project.git
- SSH shorthand: git@gitlab.example.com:group/project.git
- SSH protocol: ssh://git@gitlab.example.com/group/project.git

Returns: {id, name, path, path_with_namespace, web_url, description, default_branch, visibility, http_url_to_repo, ssh_url_to_repo, extracted_path}. Errors: 404 not found (hint: project may be private — verify token permissions), 403 forbidden (hint: token lacks read_api scope).

See also: gitlab_project (full project CRUD/settings once id is known), gitlab_server (connectivity and version checks), gitlab_search (find projects by query).

remote_url.description: Full git remote URL (HTTPS or SSH) exactly as shown in .git/config or 'git remote -v' output. IMPORTANT: pass the complete URL including the scheme (https://) or user prefix (git@). Examples: 'https://gitlab.example.com/group/project.git' or 'git@gitlab.example.com:group/project.git'. Do not pass plain project paths such as group/project, and do not synthesize URLs by adding .git to a project path; project paths are already valid project_id values.

force.description: Force stop even if environment has active deployments

name: gitlab_environment_update
description: Update an existing environment in a project. Returns: the updated environment with state, tier, external URL, cluster agent, Kubernetes namespace, Flux resource path, and auto-stop settings. See also: gitlab_environment_get, gitlab_environment_list, gitlab_environment_stop.

cluster_agent_id.description: ID of the cluster agent to associate with this environment

flux_resource_path.description: Flux resource path used to track the environment's deployment status

kubernetes_namespace.description: Kubernetes namespace for the cluster agent

tier.description: Updated tier: production, staging, testing, development, other

name: gitlab_epic_create
description:
Create a new epic in a GitLab group (via Work Items GraphQL API). Supports title, description, confidentiality, color, dates, assignees, labels, weight, and health status.

Returns: JSON with created epic details. See also: gitlab_epic_get.

full_path.description: Full path of the group (e.g. my-group)

name: gitlab_epic_delete
description:
Permanently delete an epic from a GitLab group (via Work Items GraphQL API).

Returns: JSON with deletion confirmation. See also: gitlab_epic_get.

confirm.description: Set true to explicitly confirm this destructive action instead of relying on MCP elicitation.

full_path.description: Full path of the group (e.g. my-group)

name: gitlab_epic_get
description:
Get a single group epic by its IID (via Work Items GraphQL API). Returns title, description, state, labels, dates, author, assignees, linked items, and health status.

Returns: JSON with epic details. See also: gitlab_epic_list, gitlab_epic_get_links.

full_path.description: Full path of the group (e.g. my-group)

name: gitlab_epic_get_links
description:
Get all child epics of a parent epic (via REST API). Returns the list of sub-epics linked to the specified epic.

Note: This tool uses the REST API because the Work Items GraphQL API does not yet support listing children.

Returns: JSON with child_epics array. See also: gitlab_epic_get.

full_path.description: Full path of the group (e.g. my-group)

name: gitlab_epic_issue_assign
description:
Assign an existing issue to a GitLab group epic via the Work Items GraphQL API. The issue is identified by its project path and IID.

Returns: JSON with the epic and child work item GIDs. See also: gitlab_epic_issue_list.

child_iid.description: IID of the issue to assign to the epic

child_project_path.description: Full project path of the issue to assign (e.g. my-group/my-project)

full_path.description: Full path of the group that contains the epic

name: gitlab_epic_issue_list
description:
List all child issues of a GitLab group epic via the Work Items GraphQL API. Supports cursor-based pagination.

Returns: JSON with issues array and pagination metadata. See also: gitlab_epic_get.

after.description: Cursor for forward pagination (from previous response end_cursor)

before.description: Cursor for backward pagination (from previous response start_cursor)

first.description: Number of items to return (default 20, max 100)

full_path.description: Full path of the group (e.g. my-group or my-group/sub-group)

last.description: Number of items from the end (backward pagination)

name: gitlab_epic_issue_remove
description:
Remove an issue from a GitLab group epic via the Work Items GraphQL API. Clears the child's parent reference.

Returns: JSON with the epic and child work item GIDs. See also: gitlab_epic_issue_list.

child_iid.description: IID of the issue to remove from the epic

child_project_path.description: Full project path of the issue to remove

confirm.description: Set true to explicitly confirm this destructive action instead of relying on MCP elicitation.

full_path.description: Full path of the group that contains the epic

name: gitlab_epic_issue_update
description:
Reorder an issue within a GitLab group epic via the Work Items GraphQL API. Moves the issue before or after a reference issue.

Returns: JSON with the updated issues list. See also: gitlab_epic_issue_list.

adjacent_id.description: Work item GID of the reference issue to position relative to

child_id.description: Work item GID of the issue to reorder (from list output id field)

full_path.description: Full path of the group that contains the epic

relative_position.description: Position relative to adjacent item: BEFORE or AFTER

name: gitlab_epic_list
description:
List epics for a GitLab group (via Work Items GraphQL API with type=Epic). Supports filtering by state, labels, author, search text, and cursor-based pagination.

Returns: JSON with epics array. See also: gitlab_epic_get.

first.description: Number of items to return (cursor-based pagination)

full_path.description: Full path of the group (e.g. my-group or my-group/sub-group)

name: gitlab_epic_note_create
description:
Add a comment (note) to a GitLab group epic via the Work Items GraphQL API. Supports Markdown formatting.

Returns: JSON with created note including ID, body, author, and timestamps. See also: gitlab_epic_get.

full_path.description: Full path of the group (e.g. my-group)

name: gitlab_epic_note_delete
description:
Permanently delete a comment from a GitLab group epic via the Work Items GraphQL API. Only the note author or a group maintainer can delete a note.

Returns: JSON with deletion confirmation. See also: gitlab_epic_note_get.

confirm.description: Set true to explicitly confirm this destructive action instead of relying on MCP elicitation.

full_path.description: Full path of the group (e.g. my-group)

note_id.description: ID of the note to delete

name: gitlab_epic_note_get
description:
Get a single comment (note) from a GitLab group epic by its note ID via the Work Items GraphQL API, including author, timestamps, body, and system flag.

Returns: JSON with note details including ID, body, author, and timestamps. See also: gitlab_epic_note_list.

full_path.description: Full path of the group (e.g. my-group)

note_id.description: ID of the note to retrieve

name: gitlab_epic_note_list
description:
List all comments (notes) on a GitLab group epic via the Work Items GraphQL API. Supports cursor-based pagination.

Returns: JSON with notes array including body, author, timestamps, and system flags. See also: gitlab_epic_get.

after.description: Cursor for forward pagination (from previous response end_cursor)

before.description: Cursor for backward pagination (from previous response start_cursor)

first.description: Number of items to return (default 20, max 100)

full_path.description: Full path of the group (e.g. my-group or my-group/sub-group)

last.description: Number of items from the end (backward pagination)

name: gitlab_epic_note_update
description:
Edit the body text of an existing comment on a GitLab group epic via the Work Items GraphQL API. Only the note author or a group maintainer can update a note.

Returns: JSON with updated note including ID, body, author, and timestamps. See also: gitlab_epic_note_get.

full_path.description: Full path of the group (e.g. my-group)

note_id.description: ID of the note to update

name: gitlab_epic_update
description:
Update an existing group epic (via Work Items GraphQL API). Can modify title, description, labels, state (CLOSE/REOPEN), confidentiality, parent, color, dates, assignees, weight, health status, and status.

Returns: JSON with updated epic details. See also: gitlab_epic_get.

add_label_ids.description: Global IDs of labels to add

assignee_ids.description: Global IDs of assignees (empty array to remove all)

full_path.description: Full path of the group (e.g. my-group)

parent_id.description: Global ID of the parent epic work item

remove_label_ids.description: Global IDs of labels to remove

status.description: Work item status: TODO, IN_PROGRESS, DONE, WONT_DO, or DUPLICATE

name: gitlab_feature_flag_create
description:
Create a new feature flag for a project.

Returns: JSON with created feature flag including name, active status, and strategies.

See also: gitlab_feature_flag_list, gitlab_ff_user_list_create

strategies.description: JSON array of strategy objects: [{name, parameters, scopes}]

name: gitlab_feature_flag_delete
description:
Delete a feature flag.

Returns: JSON with deletion confirmation.

See also: gitlab_feature_flag_list, gitlab_feature_flag_create

confirm.description: Set true to explicitly confirm this destructive action instead of relying on MCP elicitation.

name: gitlab_feature_flag_get
description:
Get a single feature flag by name.

Returns: JSON with feature flag details including name, active status, and strategies.

See also: gitlab_feature_flag_list, gitlab_feature_flag_update

name: gitlab_feature_flag_list
description:
List feature flags for a project.

Returns: JSON with feature flags array including name, active status, and strategies.

See also: gitlab_feature_flag_get, gitlab_ff_user_list_list

page.description: Page number to fetch, 1-based. Defaults to 1. Use the next_page field from the previous response to paginate forward.

per_page.description: Items per page. Defaults to 20, minimum 1, maximum 100. Use 100 to minimize round trips when the result set is large.

name: gitlab_feature_flag_update
description:
Update an existing feature flag.

Returns: JSON with updated feature flag including name, active status, and strategies.

See also: gitlab_feature_flag_get, gitlab_feature_flag_delete

strategies.description: JSON array of strategy objects: [{id, name, parameters, scopes}]

name: gitlab_ff_user_list_create
description:
Create a new feature flag user list.

Returns: JSON with created user list including name, IID, and user_xids.

See also: gitlab_ff_user_list_list, gitlab_feature_flag_create

user_xids.description: Comma-separated list of user external IDs

name: gitlab_ff_user_list_delete
description:
Delete a feature flag user list.

Returns: JSON with deletion confirmation.

See also: gitlab_ff_user_list_list, gitlab_feature_flag_list

confirm.description: Set true to explicitly confirm this destructive action instead of relying on MCP elicitation.

user_list_iid.description: Feature flag user list internal ID returned by list or create; do not use the user list name

name: gitlab_ff_user_list_get
description:
Get a single feature flag user list by IID.

Returns: JSON with user list details including name, IID, and user_xids.

See also: gitlab_ff_user_list_list, gitlab_feature_flag_get

user_list_iid.description: Feature flag user list internal ID returned by list or create; do not use the user list name

name: gitlab_ff_user_list_list
description:
List feature flag user lists for a project.

Returns: JSON with user lists array including name, IID, and user_xids.

See also: gitlab_ff_user_list_get, gitlab_feature_flag_list

page.description: Page number to fetch, 1-based. Defaults to 1. Use the next_page field from the previous response to paginate forward.

per_page.description: Items per page. Defaults to 20, minimum 1, maximum 100. Use 100 to minimize round trips when the result set is large.

name: gitlab_ff_user_list_update
description:
Update a feature flag user list.

Returns: JSON with updated user list including name, IID, and user_xids.

See also: gitlab_ff_user_list_get, gitlab_ff_user_list_delete

user_list_iid.description: Feature flag user list internal ID returned by list or create; do not use the user list name

user_xids.description: Comma-separated list of user external IDs

name: gitlab_file_blame
description: Get blame information for a file in a GitLab repository. Shows which commit and author last modified each line range. Supports optional line range filtering. Returns: file_path and blame ranges with commit ID, author, message, and lines. See also: gitlab_file_get, gitlab_commit_get.

file_path.description: URL-encoded full path of the file

range_end.description: End line number for blame range

range_start.description: Start line number for blame range

ref.description: Branch, tag, or commit SHA (defaults to default branch)

name: gitlab_file_create
description: Create a new file in a GitLab repository. Requires branch and commit message. Optionally specify encoding (text/base64), start_branch, and author info. Returns: file_path, branch, and current commit metadata when available. See also: gitlab_commit_create, gitlab_file_get.

branch.description: Branch to create the file on

encoding.description: Content encoding: text or base64 (default: text)

execute_filemode.description: Enable execute permission on the file

file_path.description: URL-encoded full path of the new file

start_branch.description: Branch to start from (creates new branch if different from branch)

name: gitlab_file_delete
description:
Delete a file from a GitLab repository. Requires branch and commit message. This action cannot be undone.

Returns: confirmation message. See also: gitlab_file_get.

branch.description: Branch to delete the file from

confirm.description: Set true to explicitly confirm this destructive action instead of relying on MCP elicitation.

file_path.description: URL-encoded full path of the file to delete

last_commit_id.description: Last known commit ID for optimistic locking

name: gitlab_file_get
description:
Retrieve the decoded content of a single file from a GitLab repository at a specific ref (branch name, tag name, or commit SHA). Returns file content, size, encoding, and last commit ID. This is the primary tool for reading file contents. For raw text without metadata use gitlab_file_raw. For metadata only (no content) use gitlab_file_metadata.

Returns: file_name, file_path, size, encoding, content, ref, blob_id, commit_id, and last_commit_id. See also: gitlab_file_create, gitlab_repository_tree.

file_path.description: URL-encoded full path of the file (e.g. src%2Fmain.go or src/main.go)

ref.description: Branch name, tag, or commit SHA (defaults to default branch)

name: gitlab_file_metadata
description:
Get file metadata WITHOUT retrieving content. Use this to check file existence or properties; for content use gitlab_file_get. Returns: file_name, size, encoding, blob_id, commit_id, last_commit_id, and SHA-256.

See also: gitlab_file_get.

file_path.description: URL-encoded full path of the file

ref.description: Branch, tag, or commit SHA (defaults to default branch)

name: gitlab_file_raw
description: Get the raw content of a file from a GitLab repository as plain text without metadata. Use gitlab_file_get if you also need metadata. Returns: file_path, size, and content as plain text. See also: gitlab_file_get.

file_path.description: URL-encoded full path of the file

ref.description: Branch, tag, or commit SHA (defaults to default branch)

name: gitlab_file_raw_metadata
description:
Get file metadata via HEAD request to the raw file endpoint. Returns size, encoding, blob ID, commit IDs, and SHA-256 without retrieving content. Lighter than gitlab_file_metadata — uses a HEAD request instead of GET.

Returns: file_name, size, encoding, blob_id, commit_id, last_commit_id, and SHA-256.

See also: gitlab_file_get.

file_path.description: URL-encoded full path of the file

ref.description: Branch, tag, or commit SHA (defaults to default branch)

name: gitlab_file_update
description: Update an existing file in a GitLab repository. Requires branch and commit message. Supports last_commit_id for optimistic locking. Returns: file_path, branch, and current commit metadata when available. See also: gitlab_file_get.

branch.description: Branch to update the file on

encoding.description: Content encoding: text or base64 (default: text)

execute_filemode.description: Enable execute permission on the file

file_path.description: URL-encoded full path of the file to update

last_commit_id.description: Last known commit ID for optimistic locking

name: gitlab_force_push_mirror_update
description: Trigger an immediate update of a push mirror. Returns: a confirmation that the update was triggered. See also: gitlab_get_project_mirror, gitlab_edit_project_mirror.

confirm.description: Set true to explicitly confirm this destructive action instead of relying on MCP elicitation.

name: gitlab_get_appearance
description: Get the current GitLab application appearance and branding settings. Returns: the instance appearance object including title, messages, logos, and PWA labels. See also: gitlab_update_appearance, gitlab_get_settings, gitlab_get_metadata.

name: gitlab_get_application_statistics
description: Get GitLab application statistics for the current instance. Returns: aggregate counts for users, groups, projects, issues, merge requests, and related records. See also: gitlab_get_metadata, gitlab_server_status.

name: gitlab_get_avatar
description: Get the avatar URL for an email address. Returns: the resolved avatar URL for that email address. See also: gitlab_user_current, gitlab_get_user_status.

email.description: Email address to look up avatar for

name: gitlab_get_broadcast_message
description: Get a broadcast message by id. Returns: the message with text, theme, target, and schedule. See also: gitlab_list_broadcast_messages, gitlab_update_broadcast_message.

id.description: Broadcast message ID

name: gitlab_get_bulk_import
description: Get a bulk import by id. Returns: the bulk import with status, source URL, and timestamps. See also: gitlab_list_bulk_imports, gitlab_list_bulk_import_entities.

id.description: Bulk import ID

name: gitlab_get_bulk_import_entity
description: Get a bulk import entity. Returns: the entity with source path, destination path, entity_type, and status. See also: gitlab_list_bulk_import_entities, gitlab_list_bulk_import_entity_failures.

entity_id.description: Entity ID within the bulk import

name: gitlab_get_catalog_resource
description: Get a CI/CD Catalog resource by GID or project full path. Returns: full resource details including README, released versions, components with their input parameters and include paths. See also: gitlab_list_catalog_resources, gitlab_template.

full_path.description: Full path of the project hosting the resource (e.g. my-group/my-components). Use either id or full_path.

id.description: Catalog resource GID (e.g. gid://gitlab/Ci::CatalogResource/1). Use either id or full_path.

name: gitlab_get_ci_yml_template
description:
Get a single GitLab CI YAML template by key. Returns the template name and content.

Returns: JSON with the template name and content.

See also: gitlab_list_ci_yml_templates, gitlab_ci_lint

name: gitlab_get_cluster_agent
description: Get a cluster agent. Returns: the agent with id, name, config project, and created_at. See also: gitlab_list_cluster_agents, gitlab_list_cluster_agent_tokens.

name: gitlab_get_cluster_agent_token
description: Get a cluster agent token. Returns: the token with id, name, status, and last_used_at. See also: gitlab_list_cluster_agent_tokens, gitlab_create_cluster_agent_token.

name: gitlab_get_commit_discussion
description:
Get a single discussion thread on a project commit.

Returns: JSON with discussion thread details including all notes and positions.

See also: gitlab_list_commit_discussions, gitlab_add_commit_discussion_note

name: gitlab_get_compliance_policy_settings
description:
Get the admin-level compliance policy settings for the GitLab instance.

Returns: JSON with compliance policy settings.

See also: gitlab_update_compliance_policy_settings

name: gitlab_get_custom_attribute
description: Get a custom attribute by key. Returns: the attribute with key and value. See also: gitlab_list_custom_attributes, gitlab_set_custom_attribute.

resource_type.description: Resource type: user, group, or project

name: gitlab_get_dependency_list_export
description: Check the status of a dependency list export. Returns: export ID, completion status, and download URL when ready. See also: gitlab_create_dependency_list_export, gitlab_download_dependency_list_export.

name: gitlab_get_dockerfile_template
description:
Get a single Dockerfile template by key.

Returns: JSON with the template name and content.

See also: gitlab_list_dockerfile_templates, gitlab_list_project_templates

name: gitlab_get_email
description:
Retrieve a specific email address by its ID.

See also: gitlab_list_emails_for_user, gitlab_add_email

Returns: JSON with email details.

name: gitlab_get_enterprise_user
description:
Get details of a specific enterprise user.

Returns: JSON with user details. See also: gitlab_list_enterprise_users.

name: gitlab_get_epic_discussion
description:
Get a single discussion thread on a group epic via the Work Items GraphQL API.

Returns: JSON with discussion thread details including all notes.

See also: gitlab_list_epic_discussions, gitlab_add_epic_discussion_note

full_path.description: Full path of the group (e.g. my-group)

name: gitlab_get_error_tracking_settings
description: Get error-tracking settings. Returns: the settings with active flag and integrated mode. See also: gitlab_enable_disable_error_tracking, gitlab_list_error_tracking_client_keys.

name: gitlab_get_freeze_period
description:
Get a single deploy freeze period by ID.

Returns: JSON with freeze period details including cron schedule, timezone, and status.

See also: gitlab_list_freeze_periods, gitlab_update_freeze_period

name: gitlab_get_geo_site
description:
Get configuration of a specific Geo site by ID.

Returns: JSON with Geo site configuration.

See also: gitlab_list_geo_sites, gitlab_get_status_geo_site

id.description: Numeric ID of the Geo site

name: gitlab_get_gitignore_template
description:
Get a single gitignore template by key.

Returns: JSON with the template name and content.

See also: gitlab_list_gitignore_templates, gitlab_list_project_templates

name: gitlab_get_gpg_key
description:
Retrieve a specific GPG key by its ID for the current user.

See also: gitlab_list_gpg_keys, gitlab_add_gpg_key

Returns: JSON with GPG key details.

key_id.description: The ID of the GPG key

name: gitlab_get_gpg_key_for_user
description:
Retrieve a specific GPG key for a specific user by user ID and key ID.

See also: gitlab_list_gpg_keys_for_user, gitlab_add_gpg_key_for_user

Returns: JSON with GPG key details.

key_id.description: The ID of the GPG key

name: gitlab_get_group_audit_event
description: Get a single group-level audit event by ID. Returns: audit event with ID, author, entity, event details, and created timestamp. See also: gitlab_list_group_audit_events.

name: gitlab_get_group_badge
description:
Get a specific group badge by ID.

See also: gitlab_list_group_badges, gitlab_edit_group_badge

Returns: JSON with badge details.

name: gitlab_get_group_datadog_integration
description:
Read the Datadog integration configured on a group. Requires Owner role and GitLab Premium/Ultimate (self-managed EE or GitLab.com). The api_key is never returned.

Returns: JSON with the group's Datadog integration details (api_url, datadog_env, datadog_service, datadog_site, datadog_tags, archive_trace_events).

See also: gitlab_set_group_datadog_integration, gitlab_delete_group_datadog_integration

name: gitlab_get_group_dora_metrics
description: Get DORA metrics for a GitLab group. Requires metric type (deployment_frequency, lead_time_for_changes, time_to_restore_service, change_failure_rate). Supports date range and interval filtering. Returns: list of date/value data points. See also: gitlab_get_project_dora_metrics, gitlab_environment_list.

environment_tiers.description: Filter by environment tiers (e.g. production, staging)

interval.description: Aggregation interval: daily, monthly, all (default: daily)

metric.description: DORA metric type: deployment_frequency, lead_time_for_changes, time_to_restore_service, change_failure_rate

name: gitlab_get_group_issue_statistics
description: Get issue count statistics for a group and its descendant projects. Returns: a statistics object with nested counts (all, opened, closed). See also: gitlab_get_issue_statistics, gitlab_get_project_issue_statistics, gitlab_group_get.

created_after.description: Return issues created after date (ISO 8601)

created_before.description: Return issues created before date (ISO 8601)

my_reaction_emoji.description: Filter by issues you reacted to with this emoji (or None/Any)

search.description: Search string for title and description

name: gitlab_get_group_mr_approval_settings
description:
Get group-level merge request approval settings: whether author/committer approval is allowed, approver list overrides, approval retention on push, and reauthentication requirements. Settings may be locked or inherited from parent groups.

Returns: JSON with each setting's value, locked status, and inheritance source. Requires GitLab Premium.

See also: gitlab_update_group_mr_approval_settings, gitlab_get_project_mr_approval_settings.

name: gitlab_get_group_scim_identity
description:
Get a single SCIM identity for a GitLab group by UID.

Returns: JSON with identity details. See also: gitlab_list_group_scim_identities.

uid.description: SCIM external UID of the user

name: gitlab_get_group_storage_move
description:
Get a single group repository storage move by ID (admin only).

Returns: JSON with storage move details.

See also: gitlab_get_group_storage_move_for_group

id.description: Numeric ID of the storage move

name: gitlab_get_group_storage_move_for_group
description:
Get a single repository storage move for a specific group (admin only).

Returns: JSON with storage move details.

See also: gitlab_get_group_storage_move

id.description: Numeric ID of the storage move

name: gitlab_get_impersonation_token
description:
Retrieve a specific impersonation token by user ID and token ID.

See also: gitlab_list_impersonation_tokens, gitlab_create_impersonation_token

Returns: JSON with token details.

name: gitlab_get_instance_audit_event
description: Get a single instance-level audit event by ID (admin only). Returns: audit event with ID, author, entity, event details, and created timestamp. See also: gitlab_list_instance_audit_events.

name: gitlab_get_integration
description:
Get details of a specific project integration by slug (e.g. jira, slack, discord, mattermost, microsoft-teams, telegram, datadog, jenkins, emails-on-push, pipelines-email, external-wiki, custom-issue-tracker, drone-ci, github, harbor, matrix, redmine, youtrack, slack-slash-commands, mattermost-slash-commands).

Returns: JSON with integration details.

See also: gitlab_list_integrations, gitlab_delete_integration

slug.description: Integration slug (e.g. jira, slack, discord, mattermost, microsoft-teams, telegram, emails-on-push, pipelines-email, external-wiki, custom-issue-tracker, datadog, drone-ci, github, harbor, jenkins, matrix, redmine, youtrack, slack-slash-commands, mattermost-slash-commands)

name: gitlab_get_issue_discussion
description: Get a single issue discussion thread by its discussion id. Returns: the thread with every note (author, body, system flag, resolvable/resolved state). See also: gitlab_list_issue_discussions, gitlab_add_issue_discussion_note, gitlab_issue_get.

name: gitlab_get_issue_statistics
description: Get global issue count statistics across all visible projects. Returns: a statistics object with nested counts (all, opened, closed). See also: gitlab_get_group_issue_statistics, gitlab_get_project_issue_statistics, gitlab_issue_list.

created_after.description: Return issues created after date (ISO 8601, e.g. 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z)

created_before.description: Return issues created before date (ISO 8601, e.g. 2025-12-31T23:59:59Z)

in.description: Fields the search query applies to (title, description, or title,description)

my_reaction_emoji.description: Filter by issues you reacted to with this emoji (or None/Any)

search.description: Search string for title and description

name: gitlab_get_job_token_access_settings
description: Get a project's CI/CD job token access settings. Returns: whether inbound job token access is limited to the allowlist. See also: gitlab_patch_job_token_access_settings, gitlab_list_job_token_inbound_allowlist, gitlab_list_job_token_group_allowlist.

name: gitlab_get_key_by_fingerprint
description:
Get an SSH key and its user by SSH key fingerprint (SHA256: or MD5:).

Returns: JSON with SSH key and user details.

See also: gitlab_get_key_with_user.

fingerprint.description: SSH key fingerprint (e.g. SHA256:abc123 or MD5:aa:bb:cc)

name: gitlab_get_key_with_user
description:
Get an SSH key and its associated user by key ID.

Returns: JSON with SSH key and user details.

name: gitlab_interactive_issue_create
description:
Create a GitLab issue through step-by-step prompts, with explicit confirmation before calling the GitLab API. Cancellation at any prompt aborts without creating the issue.

Input: project_id (numeric ID or URL-encoded path) selects the target project. Prompted fields are title, description, labels, confidential, and confirm. Requires permission to create issues in that project.

After invocation, the tool elicits in order:
- title (string, required) — issue title.
- description (string, optional, multi-line, Markdown) — leave empty to skip.
- labels (string, optional) — comma-separated; trimmed and deduped server-side.
- confidential (boolean, optional) — yes/no confirmation; defaults to public when declined.
- confirm (boolean, required) — final yes/no review of the assembled summary.

Behavior: cancellation/decline at any prompt aborts with no GitLab API call and no side effects. Each confirmed invocation creates ONE new issue; NON-idempotent — re-running with the same title/fields creates another issue. Side effects on success: GitLab fires issue-created webhooks and may notify issue subscribers.

When to use: human-in-the-loop issue creation. NOT for: scripted/programmatic creation — use gitlab_issue (action='create') with all fields pre-supplied.

Requires the MCP client to support the elicitation capability. If unsupported, returns a structured error naming gitlab_issue (action='create') as the alternative.

Returns: JSON with the created issue (id, issue_iid, web_url, title, state); issue_iid corresponds to GitLab's iid field.

See also: gitlab_issue.

project_id.description: Project ID or URL-encoded path where the issue will be created

iid.description: Project-scoped internal ID (the #N shown in GitLab); pass this value as issue_iid to other issue operations. Distinct from the global id.

name: gitlab_interactive_mr_create
description:
Create a GitLab merge request through step-by-step prompts, with explicit confirmation before calling the GitLab API. Cancellation at any prompt aborts without creating the MR.

Input: project_id (numeric ID or URL-encoded path) selects the target project. Prompted fields are source_branch, target_branch, title, description, labels, remove_source_branch, squash, and confirm. Requires permission to create merge requests in that project.

After invocation, the tool elicits in order:
- source_branch (string, required) — branch with the changes to merge.
- target_branch (string, required) — branch to merge into (e.g. main, develop).
- title (string, required) — MR title.
- description (string, optional, multi-line, Markdown) — leave empty to skip.
- labels (string, optional) — comma-separated; trimmed and deduped server-side.
- remove_source_branch (boolean, optional) — yes/no confirmation; default unset.
- squash (boolean, optional) — yes/no confirmation; default unset.
- confirm (boolean, required) — final yes/no review of the assembled summary.

Behavior: cancellation/decline at any prompt aborts with no GitLab API call and no side effects. Each confirmed invocation creates ONE new merge request. NON-idempotent — GitLab rejects an already-open MR for the same source_branch to target_branch in the same project as a validation failure (HTTP 422). Retries may fail with 422 instead of returning the existing MR. Confirm branch/MR state before re-running. For scripted idempotent workflows, use gitlab_merge_request (action='create') with all fields pre-supplied and handle 422 as the expected duplicate case.

When to use: human-in-the-loop MR creation. NOT for: scripted/programmatic creation — use gitlab_merge_request (action='create') with all fields pre-supplied.

Requires the MCP client to support the elicitation capability. If unsupported, returns a structured error naming gitlab_merge_request (action='create') as the alternative.

Returns: JSON with the created MR (id, merge_request_iid, web_url, title, source_branch, target_branch, state); merge_request_iid corresponds to GitLab's iid field.

See also: gitlab_merge_request, gitlab_branch.

project_id.description: Project ID or URL-encoded path where the MR will be created

name: gitlab_interactive_project_create
description:
Create a GitLab project through step-by-step prompts, with explicit confirmation before calling the GitLab API. Cancellation at any prompt aborts without creating the project except initialize_with_readme, where decline/cancel continues with false.

Input: no fields; every project detail is elicited. Requires permission to create projects for the authenticated user.

After invocation, the tool elicits in order:
- name (string, required) — project display name and (when path is omitted) URL slug.
- description (string, optional) — leave empty to skip.
- visibility (enum, required) — one of private, internal, public.
- initialize_with_readme (boolean, optional) — yes/no confirmation; explicit no, decline, or cancel continues with false.
- default_branch (string, optional) — leave empty to use the GitLab default ('main').
- confirm (boolean, required) — final yes/no review of the assembled summary.

When to use: human-in-the-loop project creation. NOT for: scripted/programmatic creation — use gitlab_project (action='create') with all fields pre-supplied.

Behavior: each successful invocation creates ONE new project after explicit user confirmation. NON-idempotent — re-running with the same project path/name can fail with 400/409. Cancellation/decline at any prompt aborts with no GitLab API call and no side effects, except initialize_with_readme where no/decline/cancel is accepted as initialize_with_readme=false. Side effects on success: GitLab may initialize a repository and notify project members.

Requires the MCP client to support the elicitation capability. If unsupported, returns a structured error naming gitlab_project (action='create') as the alternative.

Returns: JSON with the created project (id, path_with_namespace, web_url, visibility, default_branch).

See also: gitlab_project, gitlab_group.

name: gitlab_interactive_release_create
description:
Create a GitLab release through step-by-step prompts, with explicit confirmation before calling the GitLab API. Cancellation at any prompt aborts without creating the release.

Input: project_id (numeric ID or URL-encoded path) selects the target project. Prompted fields are tag_name, name, description, and confirm. Requires permission to create releases in that project.

After invocation, the tool elicits in order:
- tag_name (string, required) — must reference an existing tag in the project; create it first via gitlab_tag (action='create').
- name (string, optional) — release title; defaults to tag_name when left empty.
- description (string, optional, multi-line, Markdown) — release notes; leave empty to skip.
- confirm (boolean, required) — final yes/no review of the assembled summary.

When to use: human-in-the-loop release publishing. NOT for: CI/automated release creation — use gitlab_release (action='create') with all fields pre-supplied.

Requires the MCP client to support the elicitation capability. If unsupported, returns a structured error naming gitlab_release (action='create') as the alternative.

Behavior: each successful invocation publishes ONE new release after explicit user confirmation. NON-idempotent — re-running with the same tag returns 409 (release already exists). Cancellation/decline at any prompt aborts with no GitLab API call and no side effects. Side effects on success: GitLab fires release-created webhooks and may notify release subscribers.

Returns: JSON with the created release (tag_name, name, description, web_url).

See also: gitlab_release, gitlab_tag.

project_id.description: Project ID or URL-encoded path where the release will be created

name: gitlab_project_upload
description:
Upload a file to a GitLab project's markdown uploads area. Provide either file_path (absolute path to a local file) or content_base64 (base64-encoded content), not both. Returns a Markdown embed string (e.g. '![alt](/uploads/hash/filename)') that can be inserted into MR descriptions, note bodies, or discussion bodies.

Returns: JSON with the upload URL and Markdown embed string.

See also: gitlab_project_upload_list, gitlab_project_upload_delete

file_path.description: Absolute path to a local file on the MCP server filesystem. Alternative to content_base64 for files too large to base64-encode. Only one of file_path or content_base64 should be provided.

filename.description: Name of the file to upload (e.g. screenshot.png)

name: gitlab_release_create
description:
Create a GitLab release. If the tag_name does not exist yet, provide 'ref' (branch name or commit SHA) and GitLab will auto-create a lightweight tag — no need to call gitlab_tag_create first. Use 'tag_message' for an annotated tag. The response includes 'assets_sources' with auto-generated tar.gz and zip archive URLs — use those real URLs instead of constructing download links manually.

Returns: tag_name, name, description, author, commit, created_at, released_at, assets_sources, and assets_links. See also: gitlab_tag_create, gitlab_release_link_create.

milestones.description: Milestone titles to associate with the release

ref.description: Branch or commit SHA to create tag from when tag_name does not exist; include this when the prompt says ref/from ref

released_at.description: Date of the release in ISO 8601 format

tag_message.description: Message to use for the annotated tag (creates annotated tag instead of lightweight)

tag_name.description: Tag name associated with the release

name: gitlab_release_delete
description:
Delete a GitLab release. The underlying Git tag is preserved and not deleted.

Returns: deleted release details with tag_name, name, and description. See also: gitlab_release_list, gitlab_tag_delete.

confirm.description: Set true to explicitly confirm this destructive action instead of relying on MCP elicitation.

tag_name.description: Tag name of the release to delete

name: gitlab_release_get
description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific GitLab release by its tag name, including title, description, author, creation date, and associated assets. The response includes 'assets_sources' (auto-generated tar.gz/zip archive URLs) and 'assets_links' (manually added links such as package download URLs).

Returns: tag_name, name, description, author, commit, created_at, released_at, assets_sources, and assets_links. See also: gitlab_release_update, gitlab_release_link_list.

name: gitlab_release_latest
description:
Get the latest release for a GitLab project. Returns the most recently created release without needing to know the tag name.

Returns: tag_name, name, description, author, commit, created_at, released_at, and assets. See also: gitlab_release_list, gitlab_release_get.

name: gitlab_release_link_create
description:
Add an asset link to a GitLab release. IMPORTANT: (1) When linking to uploaded packages, use the real 'url' value returned by gitlab_package_publish — do NOT construct package URLs manually. (2) The 'name' MUST be the exact filename (e.g. 'checksums.txt.asc'), NEVER add descriptive suffixes. Consider using gitlab_package_publish_and_link instead to upload and link in one step. Supports link types: runbook, package, image, or other. Links appear in the release's assets section.

Returns: JSON with the created release link (ID, name, URL, type). See also: gitlab_release_get.

link_type.description: Type of the release link: other, runbook, image, or package.

url.description: Absolute http, https, or ftp URL of the link target. Do not use local file paths or relative paths.

name: gitlab_release_link_create_batch
description:
Add multiple asset links to a GitLab release in a single call. Use this instead of calling gitlab_release_link_create multiple times. Each link requires a name and url; link_type is optional (runbook, package, image, other). IMPORTANT: (1) For package links, use the real 'url' values returned by gitlab_package_publish. (2) Link names MUST be exact filenames — never add descriptive suffixes.

Returns: JSON with arrays of created links and any failures. See also: gitlab_release_link_list.

links.description: Array of release asset links. Each item supports only name, url, and link_type.

link_type.description: Type of the link: package, runbook, image, or other. Use package for package registry assets.

url.description: Absolute http, https, or ftp URL of the link target. For package assets, use the URL returned by gitlab_package publish actions; do not construct package URLs manually.

name: gitlab_track_event
description: Track one usage event. Returns: a success status. See also: gitlab_track_events, gitlab_get_service_ping.

send_to_snowplow.description: Whether to send event to Snowplow

name: gitlab_track_events
description: Track multiple usage events. Returns: a success status. See also: gitlab_track_event, gitlab_get_service_ping.

send_to_snowplow.description: Whether to send event to Snowplow

name: gitlab_unban_user
description:
Unban a previously banned GitLab user (admin only).

See also: gitlab_ban_user, gitlab_unblock_user

Returns: JSON with action confirmation.

name: gitlab_unblock_user
description:
Unblock a previously blocked GitLab user, restoring login and API access (admin only).

See also: gitlab_block_user, gitlab_get_user

Returns: JSON with action confirmation.

name: gitlab_unlock_terraform_state
description: Unlock a project Terraform state by project_id and state name. Returns: the state with its lock released. See also: gitlab_lock_terraform_state, gitlab_get_terraform_state, gitlab_list_terraform_states.

confirm.description: Set true to explicitly confirm this destructive action instead of relying on MCP elicitation.

name.description: Terraform state name. Use params.name for values such as production or eval-unlock-123; do not use id.

name: gitlab_update_alert_metric_image
description: Update an alert metric image. Returns: the updated metric image. See also: gitlab_list_alert_metric_images, gitlab_delete_alert_metric_image.

url.description: URL to link the metric image to

name: gitlab_update_appearance
description: Update GitLab application appearance and branding settings. Returns: the updated appearance object after GitLab applies the change. See also: gitlab_get_appearance, gitlab_get_settings, gitlab_get_metadata.

email_header_and_footer_enabled.description: Enable header and footer in emails

title.description: Application title displayed in the header

name: gitlab_update_broadcast_message
description: Update a broadcast message. Returns: the updated message. See also: gitlab_get_broadcast_message, gitlab_delete_broadcast_message.

id.description: Broadcast message ID

target_path.description: Target path to show message on

name: gitlab_update_commit_discussion_note
description:
Update an existing note in a commit discussion thread.

Returns: JSON with updated note including ID, body, and author.

See also: gitlab_get_commit_discussion, gitlab_delete_commit_discussion_note

name: gitlab_update_compliance_policy_settings
description:
Update the admin-level compliance policy settings for the GitLab instance.

Returns: JSON with updated compliance policy settings.

See also: gitlab_get_compliance_policy_settings

csp_namespace_id.description: Namespace ID for the compliance security policy project

name: gitlab_update_epic_discussion_note
description:
Update an existing note in an epic discussion thread via the Work Items GraphQL API.

Returns: JSON with updated note including ID, body, and author.

See also: gitlab_get_epic_discussion, gitlab_delete_epic_discussion_note

full_path.description: Full path of the group (e.g. my-group)

name: gitlab_update_freeze_period
description:
Update a deploy freeze period's cron schedule or timezone.

Returns: JSON with updated freeze period including ID, cron schedule, and timezone.

See also: gitlab_get_freeze_period, gitlab_delete_freeze_period

name: gitlab_update_group_mr_approval_settings
description:
Update group-level merge request approval settings: control author/committer approval, approver list overrides, approval retention on push, and reauthentication. Only include settings you want to change.

Returns: JSON with all updated settings. Requires GitLab Premium.

See also: gitlab_get_group_mr_approval_settings.

allow_author_approval.description: Allow merge request authors to approve their own MRs

allow_committer_approval.description: Allow committers to approve MRs they contributed to

allow_overrides_approver_list_per_mr.description: Allow overriding approver list per merge request

retain_approvals_on_push.description: Retain approvals when new commits are pushed

name: gitlab_update_group_scim_identity
description:
Update a SCIM identity for a GitLab group. Changes the external UID.

Returns: JSON with confirmation. See also: gitlab_get_group_scim_identity.

uid.description: SCIM external UID of the user

name: gitlab_update_group_secret_push_protection
description:
Enable or disable secret push protection for a GitLab group. Optionally exclude specific projects.

Returns: JSON with updated group security settings. See also: gitlab_get_project_security_settings.

projects_to_exclude.description: Project IDs to exclude from group-level protection

secret_push_protection_enabled.description: Enable or disable secret push protection

name: gitlab_update_instance_service_account
description: Update an instance-level service account. Returns: updated service account object including email and unconfirmed_email. Requires admin token. See also: gitlab_create_service_account, gitlab_list_service_accounts.

email.description: New email for the service account

name.description: New name for the service account

username.description: New username for the service account

name: gitlab_update_issue_discussion_note
description: Update the body of a note in an issue discussion thread. Returns: the updated note. See also: gitlab_add_issue_discussion_note, gitlab_delete_issue_discussion_note, gitlab_get_issue_discussion.

created_at.description: Override the note creation time (ISO 8601, e.g. 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z); requires admin or owner rights

name: gitlab_update_package_protection_rule
description:
Update an existing package protection rule for a GitLab project.

Returns: JSON with updated rule details. See also: gitlab_list_package_protection_rules.

minimum_access_level_for_delete.description: Minimum access level for delete (maintainer, owner, admin)

minimum_access_level_for_push.description: Minimum access level for push (maintainer, owner, admin)

package_name_pattern.description: Package name pattern with optional wildcards

package_type.description: Package type (npm, pypi, maven, generic, etc.)

name: gitlab_update_project_external_status_check
description:
Update an external status check for a project. Requires project_id and check_id. Optionally update name, external_url, shared_secret, and protected_branch_ids.

Returns: updated status check with ID, name, external URL, HMAC, protected branches. See also: gitlab_list_project_external_status_checks.

check_id.description: External status check ID to update

shared_secret.description: Updated shared secret for HMAC verification

name: gitlab_update_project_mr_approval_settings
description:
Update project-level merge request approval settings: control author/committer approval, approver list overrides, approval retention on push, selective code owner removals, and reauthentication. Only include settings you want to change.

Returns: JSON with all updated settings. Requires GitLab Premium.

See also: gitlab_get_project_mr_approval_settings.

allow_author_approval.description: Allow merge request authors to approve their own MRs

allow_committer_approval.description: Allow committers to approve MRs they contributed to

allow_overrides_approver_list_per_mr.description: Allow overriding approver list per merge request

retain_approvals_on_push.description: Retain approvals when new commits are pushed

selective_code_owner_removals.description: Only remove Code Owner approvals for changed files (project-only)

name: gitlab_update_project_secret_push_protection
description:
Enable or disable secret push protection for a GitLab project.

Returns: JSON with updated security settings. See also: gitlab_get_project_security_settings.

secret_push_protection_enabled.description: Enable or disable secret push protection

name: gitlab_update_project_security_attributes
description: Add or remove GitLab security attributes on a project via GraphQL. Requires Premium or Ultimate. Returns: project security attribute assignments. See also: gitlab_security_attribute, gitlab_project. API docs: https://docs.gitlab.com/api/graphql/reference/#mutationsecurityattributeprojectupdate

confirm.description: Set true to explicitly confirm this destructive action instead of relying on MCP elicitation.

name: gitlab_update_repository_submodule
description:
Update an existing submodule reference in a GitLab repository to point to a new commit SHA.

Returns: JSON with the updated submodule reference.

See also: gitlab_list_repository_submodules

branch.description: Branch name to commit the update to

commit_sha.description: Full commit SHA to update the submodule to

submodule.description: URL-encoded full path to the submodule

name: gitlab_update_security_attribute
description: Update a GitLab security attribute name, description, or color via GraphQL. Requires Premium or Ultimate. Returns: updated security attribute metadata. See also: gitlab_security_category, gitlab_project, gitlab_group. API docs: https://docs.gitlab.com/api/graphql/reference/#mutationsecurityattributeupdate

color.description: New security attribute color as a hex code (e.g. #FF0000)

name: gitlab_update_security_category
description: Update a GitLab security category name or description via GraphQL. Requires Premium or Ultimate. Returns: updated security category. See also: gitlab_security_attribute, gitlab_group, gitlab_project. API docs: https://docs.gitlab.com/api/graphql/reference/#mutationsecuritycategoryupdate

name: gitlab_update_settings
description: Update GitLab application settings. Returns: the full updated application settings object. See also: gitlab_get_settings, gitlab_update_appearance.

settings.description: Map of setting_name to new value. Use snake_case keys matching GitLab API fields (e.g. signup_enabled, default_project_visibility, max_artifacts_size).

name: gitlab_update_snippet_discussion_note
description:
Update an existing note in a snippet discussion thread.

Returns: JSON with the updated note details.

See also: gitlab_get_snippet_discussion, gitlab_delete_snippet_discussion_note

name: gitlab_update_topic
description: Update a project topic. Returns: the updated topic. See also: gitlab_get_topic, gitlab_delete_topic.

name: gitlab_update_work_item
description:
Update an existing work item by IID. Supports changing title, state (CLOSE/REOPEN), description, assignees, milestone, labels (add/remove), dates, weight, health status, iteration, color, and status (TODO/IN_PROGRESS/DONE/WONT_DO/DUPLICATE). Experimental: the Work Items API may introduce breaking changes between minor versions.

Returns: JSON with the updated work item details.

See also: gitlab_get_work_item, gitlab_delete_work_item

add_label_ids.description: Global IDs of labels to add

assignee_ids.description: Global IDs of assignees (empty array to remove all)

crm_contact_ids.description: CRM contact IDs (empty array to remove all)

full_path.description: Full path of the project or group (e.g. my-group/my-project)

parent_id.description: Global ID of the parent work item

remove_label_ids.description: Global IDs of labels to remove

status.description: Work item status: TODO, IN_PROGRESS, DONE, WONT_DO, or DUPLICATE

name: gitlab_upload_alert_metric_image
description: Upload an alert metric image. Returns: the uploaded metric image with id, filename, and url. See also: gitlab_list_alert_metric_images, gitlab_update_alert_metric_image.

content_base64.description: Base64-encoded image content. Only one of file_path or content_base64 should be provided.

file_path.description: Absolute path to a local image file on the MCP server filesystem. Alternative to content_base64. Only one of file_path or content_base64 should be provided.

url.description: URL to link the metric image to

name: gitlab_user_contribution_event_list
description:
List contribution events for the authenticated user. Supports filtering by action type, target type, date range, sort order, scope, and pagination.

Returns: JSON array of contribution events with pagination.

See also: gitlab_project_event_list, gitlab_get_current_user

action.description: Filter by action type (created, updated, closed, reopened, pushed, commented, merged, joined, left, destroyed, expired)

page.description: Page number for pagination (default 1)

per_page.description: Number of items per page (default 20, max 100)

scope.description: Include events from all projects (all) or only user's projects

target_type.description: Filter by target type (issue, milestone, merge_request, note, project, snippet, user)

name: gitlab_user_current
description: Get the current authenticated user. Returns: account ID, username, name, state, avatar URL, and profile metadata. See also: gitlab_list_users, gitlab_current_user_status, gitlab_list_emails.

name: gitlab_vulnerability_severity_count
description: Get vulnerability severity counts for a project (requires Ultimate/Premium). Returns: counts per severity level (critical, high, medium, low, info, unknown) and total. See also: gitlab_list_vulnerabilities, gitlab_pipeline_security_summary.

project_path.description: Full path of the project (e.g. my-group/my-project)

name: gitlab_wiki_create
description:
Create a new wiki page in a GitLab project. Supports Markdown (default), RDoc, AsciiDoc, and Org formats.

Returns: JSON with created wiki page including title, slug, and content. See also: gitlab_wiki_get.

content.description: Content of the wiki page (Markdown, RDoc, AsciiDoc, or Org)

format.description: Content format: markdown (default), rdoc, asciidoc, or org

name: gitlab_wiki_delete
description:
Delete a wiki page by slug. This action cannot be undone. Use gitlab_wiki_list to find available page slugs.

Returns: JSON with deletion confirmation. See also: gitlab_wiki_list.

confirm.description: Set true to explicitly confirm this destructive action instead of relying on MCP elicitation.

slug.description: URL-encoded slug of the wiki page to delete

name: gitlab_wiki_get
description:
Get a single wiki page by slug. Set render_html=true to get HTML-rendered content. Set version to a commit SHA to retrieve a specific historical version of the page. Use gitlab_wiki_list to discover available page slugs.

Returns: JSON with wiki page content, title, slug, format, and encoding. See also: gitlab_wiki_update.

render_html.description: Return HTML-rendered content instead of raw format

slug.description: URL-encoded slug of the wiki page (e.g. 'my-page')

version.description: Wiki page version SHA to retrieve a specific revision

name: gitlab_wiki_list
description:
List all wiki pages in a GitLab project. Optionally include page content by setting with_content=true.

Returns: JSON with wiki pages array including title, slug, format, and encoding. See also: gitlab_wiki_get, gitlab_wiki_create.

with_content.description: Include page content in the response

name: gitlab_wiki_update
description:
Update an existing wiki page by slug. Can change the title, content, and format. At least one of title, content, or format must be provided.

Returns: JSON with updated wiki page including title, slug, and content. See also: gitlab_wiki_get.

content.description: New content for the wiki page

format.description: Content format: markdown, rdoc, asciidoc, or org

slug.description: URL-encoded slug of the wiki page to update

title.description: New title for the wiki page

name: gitlab_wiki_upload_attachment
description:
Upload a file attachment to a project wiki. Provide file content as base64 or a local file path.

Returns: JSON with file path and Markdown embed snippet. See also: gitlab_wiki_create.

branch.description: Branch to upload the attachment to

content_base64.description: Base64-encoded file content. Provide either content_base64 or file_path

file_path.description: Absolute path to a local file. Provide either file_path or content_base64

filename.description: Name of the file to upload (e.g. diagram.png)
